question.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$*

current_example.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=6{x}_{1}(t)+7{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_1=-1$ and $\lambda_2=3.$*
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)$ for the given system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/31f1715583fd00d93f86fcd71026e05aae673ca8f145578c12c56260e977fe44.svg)

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are 

$$
\lambda_1=-1
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\lambda_2=3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1 =-1,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/17349e1560fd444737f6011a0492507d36b51dd9de0cda3a76b193dc35ce5188.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/7a7d2f64367530ed79755cad797bdf1f7c4f59faa74ccbf14f72f3b57442d025.svg)

- For $\lambda_2 =3,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/58d3d93ea3acf0669464dda88b80c39da812d59e8d238ae26659c8073c196566.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/64588e51190852723f26eb44346eb43ac650f2a96512eb29d632488b6af909bc.svg)

Thus, the general solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$
